{
  "ideas": [
    {
      "name": "Tissue Consensus Voting",
      "levels": ["cell", "tissue"],
      "mechanism": "Each frame region is a 'cell' with its own Jev evaluator. Instead of one VLM judging full projection fidelity, we ask Jev 50 typed questions per region (edge continuity, motion coherence, glyph legibility). Regions self-organize into 'tissues'—adjacent cells whose Jev scores correlate—by local majority vote on whether to merge. Tissues recursively vote their confidence upward. Final scene reconstruction uses only tissue-consensus projections.",
      "jev_role": "noul: 'does this region's edge flow match its neighbor's?', score: 'projection clarity 1-5 for this local patch', choice: 'which of 4 motion directions best explains these arrows'",
      "hypothesis": "A tissue of 7+ regions with internal agreement >0.85 will match ground truth within 0.05 of the three-VLM average, but 3× cheaper. Confirmed if tissue-consensus projection fidelity ≥0.30 (vs 0.34 edge-glyph baseline) using <500 Jev calls total.",
      "cost": "400-600 Jev calls (~$0.08), zero vision model calls for scoring",
      "beyond_classic_ml": "No gradient flows globally; structure emerges from peer-validated local typed judgments without a loss function over the whole image."
    },
    {
      "name": "Organ Competition with Quantum Arbitration",
      "levels": ["tissue", "organ"],
      "mechanism": "Three 'organ' projector variants (edge-glyph, motion-arrow, hybrid) each spawn tissues that grow by Jev-validated mutual aid. When organs conflict on a region's label, MothQuantum provides certified random bytes to select which organ 'innervates' that patch this frame. Jev scores the resulting mosaic; organs accrete territory where they win. Held-out frames test whether territory-boundaries generalize.",
      "jev_role": "score: 'how consistent is this mosaic with physical scene dynamics 1-5', noul: 'does organ A's label here contradict organ B's label there?', choice: 'which organ's history predicts this held-out region best'",
      "hypothesis": "After 200 frames, the mosaic organ (not any pure organ) achieves fidelity >0.40, and its territorial map on held-out frames correlates >0.7 with map from training frames. Falsified if mosaic ≤ best single organ or correlation <0.5.",
      "cost": "300 Jev calls per frame eval + 50 quantum bytes/frame, ~$0.15/frame",
      "beyond_classic_ml": "Competing specialized modules arbitrate via irreducible randomness and typed peer review, not softmax gating or differentiable mixture-of-experts."
    },
    {
      "name": "Family Lineage of Projector Kernels",
      "levels": ["organism", "family"],
      "mechanism": "Each projector config is an 'organism' with byte-exact C kernel (deterministic reproduction). Organisms reproduce with Jev-guided mutation: Jev scores whether a single-kernel-parameter change 'improves' a held-out frame's reconstruction without running full VLM. Families are lineages sharing >90% bytecode. A 'family council'—Jev choice among ancestor, parent, child configs—decides which kernel seeds next generation.",
      "jev_role": "noul: 'does this mutation preserve edge-continuity better than parent?', score: 'expected scene-reconstruction quality if this kernel were evaluated by VLM 1-5', choice: 'which of these 3 related kernels deserves to reproduce based on lineage performance'",
      "hypothesis": "Family-council selection reaches fidelity 0.45 in 50 generations; random mutation with global VLM scoring reaches 0.38 in same compute. Confirmed if family-method exceeds 0.42 and finds the improvement 2 generations faster.",
      "cost": "2000 Jev calls for lineage tracking + 100 VLM evaluations for ground-truth verification only",
      "beyond_classic_ml": "Evolution operates on typed aesthetic judgments of local patches, not fitness from end-to-end backprop; lineage memory substitutes for gradient memory."
    },
    {
      "name": "Community Protocol for Disagreement",
      "levels": ["community"],
      "mechanism": "Multiple 'species' of critics—Jev-only texture analysts, cheap VLMs (Gemma-3), full VLMs (Qwen3-VL)—form a community with no central arbiter. When species disagree on a projection's fidelity, Jev mediates a structured 'disagreement protocol': it types probabilities for which species is hallucinating based on internal consistency, not ground truth access. Community updates its 'trust weights' per species locally per frame. Resulting consensus predictions feed back to projector search.",
      "jev_role": "noul: 'is species A internally consistent across its 5 patch judgments?', score: 'trustworthiness of species B this frame 1-5', choice: 'which species' explanation better respects physical constraints (occlusion, lighting)'",
      "hypothesis": "Community consensus with Jev-mediated trust-updating achieves 0.55 fidelity when full VLMs are included 10% of time, versus 0.50 when full VLMs aggregated uniformly. Falsified if community ≤ uniform or if Jev mediation increases cost >20% without gain.",
      "cost": "500 Jev calls + 50 Gemma-3 + 10 Qwen3-VL per evaluation batch",
      "beyond_classic_ml": "Multiple model 'species' negotiate trust through typed meta-judgments about each other's coherence, not ensemble averaging or learned gating; no single model sees others' internals."
    }
  ]
}

request.content:
We have a working research harness that turns a camera feed (short frame sequences) into plain text ("projections": character art with edge glyphs, braille, motion arrows). A vision-language model reconstructs the scene (objects, positions, motion) from the text alone; agreement with ground truth is the projection's fidelity. We measured: brightness-only text 0.18, edge glyphs following edges 0.34, motion arrows over edges 0.33 with motion recall 0.27, a VLM reading the real frames 0.92. Search over projector configs is noise-limited; averaging three VLM critics and promoting on held-out feeds fixed overfitting.

Tools available right now, all via API:
- TypeSafe "Jev": a SYSTEM-ONE model that answers TYPED questions about any state (text or JSON) in ~150 ms: noul (probability yes/no), choice (pick one named option, with probabilities), score (expected value on a rubric of levels). Many named questions can be asked in ONE request about the same state. Very cheap. It cannot see images.
- DeepInfra: vision-language models (Qwen3-VL, Gemma-3, Mistral-Small), large LLMs (Kimi-K2.6, Qwen3-235B, gpt-oss-120b, MiniMax-M3, DeepSeek), CLIP / text embeddings.
- MothQuantum: certified quantum random bytes (slow on real hardware, fast in simulator).
- Everything deterministic in the projector kernel is byte-exact integer C, so any device reproduces it.

The research vision: go beyond classic RL / neural nets / backprop. Learning as a HOLARCHY of first-person perspectives — cells -> tissues -> organs -> organisms -> families -> communities — with no central authority: a murmuration or kaleidoscope of many cheap viewpoints that see reality from different angles, help each other locally, and grow structure (guided growth) rather than being trained end-to-end. Typed system-one judgments are the "nerve impulses"; expensive models are rare "deliberations".

Propose 4 CONCRETE, NOVEL experiments that can be run THIS WEEK with exactly these tools on this projection problem (we have ground truth, so results are measurable). Each must use Jev in an essential, non-trivial way, name the level(s) of organization it lives at, and state a falsifiable hypothesis with the number that would confirm or refute it. Prefer ideas where many cheap local typed judgments replace one expensive global one, where structure grows, or where perspectives negotiate without a center.

Reply with JSON only:
{"ideas": [{"name": "<short>", "levels": ["cell"|"tissue"|"organ"|"organism"|"family"|"community"], "mechanism": "<3-5 sentences>", "jev_role": "<what Jev is asked, typed>", "hypothesis": "<falsifiable, with the measurement>", "cost": "<API calls estimate>", "beyond_classic_ml": "<one sentence: why this is not just RL/NN/backprop>"}]}
